solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perform vocally in angry speech, having a quarrel

indicators.note: 'in' places the singing inside the phrase for angry speech

blocks.note: cross words are angry words exchanged
to sing is to perform with the voice

explanation.surface: Someone launches into song in the middle of a furious tirade during a row.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion point falls mid-word, splitting the angry phrase after its fourth letter, so the join hides the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom for arguing or clashing with someone.

clue.text: Have buyer's remorse, say, getting money back on wrong denims

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of their proper order and must be rearranged

blocks.note: change is the money handed back after paying
taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopper regrets buying jeans and gets a refund on the ill-fitting denims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money back' sounds like a refund, but here it is the change you receive after paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Buyer's remorse is one example of reconsidering a decision, hence the 'say'.

clue.text: Set up company on time, and work for influential organisation

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'set up' lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
T is the abbreviation for time
an opus is a work, especially of music

explanation.surface: Founding a firm on schedule and working for a powerful body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply means after, placing T after the turned-round CO.
explanation.definitionFit: An octopus is used figuratively for an organisation with far-reaching tentacles of influence.

clue.text: Unfriendly resistance put up by school?

blocks.note: surface reading: a school making a stand against something
setter's reading: a school is a shoal, so this is a stand-off staged by a group of fish

explanation.surface: A school's staff refuse to cooperate, which looks rather cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as STAND-OFF-ISH and imagine fish in a stand-off; the question mark flags the pun on school.
explanation.definitionFit: Standoffish means aloof and cold in manner, which is unfriendly.

clue.text: Making an observation — husband's not in love

indicators.note: 'not in' says this letter is absent from the word that follows, so it is taken out

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
love means nil or nothing, as in a tennis score

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the husband is no longer in love.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H from NOTHING. The 's is 'is': the husband is not in love.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting means remarking on or observing something.

clue.text: In plot of movie, for instance, one car is wrecked

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An action film's storyline in which a car gets smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' does double duty in the surface but its letters belong to the anagram fodder with one car.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is the outline of a film's story, one example of a plot.

clue.text: Product of mine often found in foreign stores — for euros, moreover

indicators.note: 'found in' says the letters sit inside other words, and 'often' says they do so several times here

blocks.note: surface padding: both words also contain the three letters, which is the joke of 'often'
sits across the end of for and the start of euros
surface padding: this word too holds the same three letters

explanation.surface: Mined goods are sold in shops abroad, priced in euros.
explanation.walkthrough: The three letters also appear inside foreign, stores and moreover, which is why the clue says often.
explanation.definitionFit: Ore is the rock dug from a mine to extract metal.

clue.text: Prolong no-win situation before striking

blocks.note: a draw is a result where nobody wins
workers who are out are on strike

explanation.surface: A deadlock drags on before the workers walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' here is industrial action, not hitting or impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out a meeting or process is to make it last longer.

clue.text: Piece of furniture and part of trunk belonging to some artists

blocks.note: the trunk is the torso, and the chest is its upper part
of expresses belonging
people who draw are drawers, one kind of artist

explanation.surface: An item of furniture plus a section of a travelling trunk owned by painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' suggests luggage, which fits the furniture theme, but it is the body's torso.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers is a cabinet of sliding storage compartments for clothes.

clue.text: Pull from that cart, take in the opposite direction

indicators.note: 'from' says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows
reading in the opposite direction means going right to left instead

blocks.note: the letters running from the last of that to the first two of take

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a load off a wagon and drags it back the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, as a magnet pulls iron.

clue.text: Bunk made from European wood (two sorts)

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
yew is one sort of tree and timber
ash is a second sort of wood, as the bracket asks

explanation.surface: A bunk bed built from two kinds of continental timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed, which suits the wood, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash and bunk are both informal words for nonsense or humbug.

clue.text: Opening gambit's beginning with a pawn

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter alone

blocks.note: the first letter of gambit
taken as written
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess opening move that starts by advancing a pawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening gambit' reads as one chess phrase, but Opening is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an opening or space between things.

clue.text: Solution for someone with bit between their teeth?

definitions.text: Solution for someone with bit between their teeth?

blocks.clueFragment: someone with bit between their teeth
blocks.note: surface reading: a determined person, like a horse taking the bit and charging on
setter's reading: a scrap of food literally stuck between the teeth, needing a dental remedy

explanation.surface: Advice for a person who is single-minded and determined.
explanation.walkthrough: To have the bit between your teeth is an idiom for being determined; read literally, it is food lodged in the gaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Dental floss is thread used to clean out debris trapped between teeth.

clue.text: Flammable material in sack on barge

blocks.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: Combustible stuff stored in a bag aboard a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sack' looks like a bag holding the material, but it is the verb meaning dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A firelighter is a block of combustible substance used to start a fire.

clue.text: You may get it from boss if you become inflexible

indicators.note: getting something from the following words means lifting a run of letters straight out of them

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of boss to the first of you

explanation.surface: A warning that a rigid manager will rub off on you if you stiffen up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ossify is literally to turn to bone, figuratively to grow rigid in habits.

clue.text: Awfully brittle old book

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An ancient volume whose pages have become terribly fragile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is not a volume but the words of an opera or musical, a sense also used for 'the book' of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera, which in theatre is called its book.

clue.text: Around area, shows signs of radioactive emissions

indicators.note: 'Around' means the following verb's letters wrap about the area letter

blocks.note: to betray is to reveal or show signs of something
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A survey of the district shows evidence of radiation leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is front-loaded: 'Around area' tells you to put A inside the word for shows signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta rays are streams of electrons given off by some radioactive nuclei.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher summoned and brought out

blocks.note: in the Bible, the priest Eli raised and taught the boy Samuel
to cite someone is to summon them to court

explanation.surface: The prophet's mentor was called and led out.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out a response or information from someone.

clue.text: Result of counting from one to e.g. ten, perhaps? Right

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters before it are only one possible arrangement, so rearrange them

blocks.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Counting up from one to ten and checking the answer is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from one to e.g. ten' means add I to EGTEN before rearranging; the surface hints that ten is itself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting things always yields a whole number, which is an integer.

clue.text: Very happy story backed by editor

indicators.note: something backed goes into reverse, so the word reads right to left

blocks.note: a tale is a story
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A writer is overjoyed that an editor supports the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like supported, but it turns the story word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means thrilled or overjoyed.

clue.text: With perfect exactness, including copy with a piece of music

indicators.note: 'including' means the phrase before it takes the following letters inside itself

blocks.note: to a T means exactly right
CC is carbon copy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A precise transcription of a musical work, with a duplicate included.
explanation.walkthrough: To a T is an idiom for exactly; CC, for carbon copy, survives from typewriter days as the copy line on an email.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard composition, such as Bach's famous one in D minor.

clue.text: Some goals I established for the rest of the day

indicators.note: 'Some' asks for only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: runs from the end of goals through I into the start of established

explanation.surface: Someone has set targets for themselves for the remainder of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest of the day' reads as the remaining hours, but it means a rest taken during the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a daytime rest common in hot countries.

clue.text: For example, test maiden and a powerful male forming a relationship

blocks.note: a Test is one example of a cricket match
M is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a maiden over
taken as written
a king is a powerful man

explanation.surface: A trial pairing of a young woman and a mighty man to see if they suit.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; 'maiden' looks like a young woman but is the cricket term for a scoreless over.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchmaking is arranging romantic pairings, setting up couples.

clue.text: Either cold meat or fish, mostly, for tea

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most of the word but not all, so its final letter is dropped

blocks.note: surface padding offering an alternative route: C for cold plus most of ham gives the same three letters
char is a fish related to the trout

explanation.surface: A choice of cold cuts or a fish dish served at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either' is honest: both halves of the clue lead to the same three letters, so the solver may take whichever route they spot first.
explanation.definitionFit: Cha, or char, is British slang for tea, from the Chinese word.

clue.text: Land in Africa I regain, in disarray

indicators.note: things in disarray are jumbled out of order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recovers territory in Africa amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a country in West Africa, the continent's most populous.

clue.text: Capsized sailor that gets out of stricken vessel

definitions.text: that gets out of stricken vessel

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, and in a down entry that turns the word over

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An overturned seaman who abandons a sinking ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are proverbially the first to desert a sinking ship, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The rodent is described by its proverbial habit of fleeing a ship in trouble.

clue.text: Used a perch I consumed to fill up

blocks.note: to use a perch is to sit on it
taken as written
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: A bird on a perch eats until full.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy hunger completely, to fill someone up.

clue.text: Rival of Aer Lingus that could make Irish a bit wary, heading south

indicators.note: 'could make' says these letters can be made into something else by rearranging them

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
S is the abbreviation for south, added at the end

explanation.surface: A competitor airline makes Irish travellers nervous as it flies south.
explanation.walkthrough: Aer Lingus is Ireland's national airline.
explanation.definitionFit: British Airways is the UK flag carrier, competing with Aer Lingus on routes between Britain and Ireland.
